title: NCBI RefSeq annotated gene-to-trait map

change_log.correction: Replaced mmol/s uptake values that implied sub-microsecond biomass doublings with per-cell channel rates derived from the table's explicit division-mass, division-hazard, biomass-fraction, and substrate molar-mass calibration. Removed the unsupported lacY-to-division-rate increment; ptsG is the sole division-rate proxy in this calibration.

feature_policy: Only annotated gene/CDS features are read. No sequence-motif scanning, fuzzy product matching, transcript expression inference, or mutation is performed.
approximation_notice: The listed gene annotations justify qualitative trait potential only. Numeric baselines/effects and bounds are explicit simulation calibration coefficients, not measured expression, uptake, growth, motility, division, or killing rates. Effects are summed in stable rule_id order and clamped to the explicit bounds. A multi-gene biosynthetic rule fires once only when all specified annotated CDS features exist. Uptake is calibrated per sole available carbon channel to the model division hazard; it is not a measured species-specific uptake capacity, and simultaneous saturated channels may sum above that single-channel calibration.

uptake_division_calibration.status: explicit internal simulation calibration; not an experimentally measured flux
uptake_division_calibration.uptake_scope: per cell, per nutrient channel, in mmol/s; not a population-level rate
uptake_division_calibration.model_assumption: For a single nutrient channel at its max uptake, biomass production is calibrated to division_mass_pg * division_rate_s. The division_rate_s value is a simulation hazard parameter, not a measured doubling rate. Other nutrients are assumed unavailable during this single-channel calibration.
uptake_division_calibration.unit_derivation: biomass_mmol * molar_mass_g_mol * 1e9 = mass_pg, matching src/microbiome/sim/engine.py::_derive_mass; therefore mmol/s is required for max_uptake_mmol_s.
limitations: The coefficients are derived from the simulation's mass conversion and chosen division calibration, not fitted biological uptake data.

Assay QA finding kb_mvc59d7hEc6dBMViUn24 reports a condition-specific E. coli B/r carbon-balance range of approximately 8e-16 to 3e-15 mmol/s per cell (280 fg dry mass, aerobic glucose minimal medium, 37 C, 40 min doubling, assumed 50% dry-mass carbon); it is not applied to MG1655, B. subtilis 168, lactose, or a maximum-capacity claim.
The zero B. subtilis lactose baseline means no lactose-specific mapping is currently curated in this table; it is not evidence that the strain lacks every lactose uptake route.

Each nutrient channel is calibrated as the sole available carbon source. If multiple channels are simultaneously saturated, their separate per-channel maxima can sum above this single-channel target; this is a documented model limitation, not a shared uptake ceiling.
